Task 1 — Exploratory Data Analysis¶

Cross-venue liquidation signal on Binance/Bybit perpetuals · Team Griffin¶

Universe: perp:btcusdt, perp:ethusdt Period: 2025-12-01 → 2026-02-28 (90 days) Streams: Binance trades, Binance booktickers (BBO/L1), Binance liquidations, Bybit liquidations.

Executive summary (read this first)¶

We profile 1.1 billion Binance trade prints, 207 M BBO updates and 0.6 M cross-venue liquidation events. Six findings drive the rest of the project:

  1. The maker is adversely selected — gross. Mid-to-mid (pre-rebate) markout is negative at every horizon (≈ −0.5 bps): a passive maker is systematically picked off. The +0.5 bps rebate nearly offsets it, so net markout is near zero — slightly negative at 30 s (≈ −0.06 bps pooled) and slightly positive at 120/300 s (≈ +0.02 / +0.08) — atop enormous cross-sectional dispersion. The game is therefore selecting the right fills, not average edge.
  2. The book is one tick wide ~95 % of the time. BTC/ETH perps sit at a 1-tick spread almost always; spread widening is a rare, information-rich regime that clusters with volatility and liquidations.
  3. Liquidations are violently clustered & heavy-tailed. Inter-arrival times are far from Poisson; a handful of cascade minutes carry most of the forced volume — a textbook self-exciting (Hawkes) process.
  4. Liquidation pressure is directional, and absorbing it pays. Trades the maker fills in the same direction as recent liquidation pressure (selling into forced buying) earn better forward markout — the cascade over-shoots and mean-reverts. This post-cascade mean-reversion is the causal seed of Task 2/3.
  5. Strong time-of-day & funding structure. Activity, volatility and liquidations peak around the US session and the 00/08/16 UTC funding stamps; markout is regime-dependent, not stationary.
  6. Bybit leads Binance by a measurable lag. Bybit liquidation bursts precede Binance mid moves, which (after the mandated +200 ms availability lag) is a genuine, usable cross-venue signal.

Limitations: L1-only book (no depth beyond top), no funding-rate/open-interest series, 3-month window (one macro regime), markout is a frictionless mid-to-mid PnL (no queue, latency or partial-fill model). Details and caveats at the end.

# --- Load compact artifacts produced by the streaming factory (one causal pass) -----
daily = pd.read_parquet(f"{ART}/daily_agg.parquet")
daily["day"] = pd.to_datetime(daily["day"], utc=True)
samp = {s: pd.read_parquet(f"{ART}/sample_trades_{s}.parquet") for s in meta["symbols"]}
for s in samp: samp[s]["dt"] = cc.to_datetime(samp[s]["timestamp"].to_numpy())

# raw liquidation tapes are small — load them in full
def load_liq(venue, sym):
    p = (f"{DATA}/binance_liquidations/perp_{sym}.parquet" if venue=="binance"
         else f"{DATA}/bybit_liquidations/{sym}.parquet")
    df = pd.read_parquet(p)
    df["dt"] = cc.to_datetime(df["timestamp"].to_numpy())
    df["notional"] = df["price"]*df["amount"]
    df["venue"] = venue
    return df
liq = {(v,s): load_liq(v,s) for v in ["binance","bybit"] for s in meta["symbols"]}
print("Sample trades:", {s: len(samp[s]) for s in samp})
print("Liquidation events:", {f"{v}/{s}": len(liq[(v,s)]) for (v,s) in liq})
print("Days per split:", daily.groupby('split')['day'].nunique().to_dict())

1.1.1 Data quality: schema, dtypes, missing values, duplicates, timestamp consistency¶

In [4]:
# Trades/BBO are hundreds of millions of rows, so stream-wide stats come from parquet
# metadata + row-group reads (cheap); exact dup/monotonic checks run on a full day below.
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
rows = []
for sym in meta["symbols"]:
    for stream,fn in [("trades",f"binance_trades/perp_{sym}"),
                      ("bbo",f"binance_booktickers/perp_{sym}"),
                      ("liq_binance",f"binance_liquidations/perp_{sym}"),
                      ("liq_bybit",f"bybit_liquidations/{sym}")]:
        pf = pq.ParquetFile(f"{DATA}/{fn}.parquet"); ng = pf.metadata.num_row_groups
        t0 = pf.read_row_group(0, columns=['timestamp']).column('timestamp')[0].as_py()
        t1 = pf.read_row_group(ng-1, columns=['timestamp']).column('timestamp')[-1].as_py()
        # cross-row-group monotonicity via per-RG min/max statistics (no full scan)
        try:
            mx=[pf.metadata.row_group(g).column(0).statistics.max for g in range(ng)]
            mn=[pf.metadata.row_group(g).column(0).statistics.min for g in range(ng)]
            rg_sorted = all(mx[g] <= mn[g+1] for g in range(ng-1))
        except Exception:
            rg_sorted = "n/a"
        rows.append(dict(symbol=sym, stream=stream, rows=pf.metadata.num_rows, n_rowgroups=ng,
                         t0=cc.to_datetime([t0])[0], t1=cc.to_datetime([t1])[0], rg_sorted=rg_sorted))
audit = pd.DataFrame(rows)
audit["rows_str"] = audit["rows"].map(lambda x: f"{x:,}")
display(audit[["symbol","stream","rows_str","n_rowgroups","t0","t1","rg_sorted"]])

# True row-duplicate & NaN check on one full representative day (2026-01-15) per stream
day = int(pd.Timestamp("2026-01-15", tz="UTC").value//1000)
qa = []
for sym in meta["symbols"]:
    paths = st.data_paths(DATA, sym)
    tr, bbo, lB, lY = st.read_day(paths, day, preroll_us=0, post_us=0)
    for name, df in [("trades",tr),("bbo",bbo),("liqB",lB),("liqY",lY)]:
        full_dup = int(df.duplicated().sum())
        mono = bool((df["timestamp"].values[1:] >= df["timestamp"].values[:-1]).all())
        qa.append(dict(symbol=sym, stream=name, rows=len(df), monotonic=mono,
                       exact_dup_rows=full_dup, dup_ts_frac=round(float(df["timestamp"].duplicated().mean()),3),
                       any_nan=int(df.isna().any().any())))
    # BBO sanity: crossed/locked books, non-positive sizes
    cross = int((bbo['ask_price']<=bbo['bid_price']).sum())
    qa.append(dict(symbol=sym, stream="bbo:crossed_or_locked", rows=len(bbo),
                   exact_dup_rows=cross, any_nan=int((bbo[['bid_amount','ask_amount']]<=0).any().any())))
display(pd.DataFrame(qa))

1.2.3 Non-linearities — conditional markout vs candidate predictors¶

In [12]:
def cond_markout(s, col, tau=30, q=12, wcol="w", clip=None):
    d=s[[col,f"pnl_{tau}",wcol]].dropna()
    if clip: d=d[(d[col]>=d[col].quantile(clip[0]))&(d[col]<=d[col].quantile(clip[1]))]
    d["bin"]=pd.qcut(d[col].rank(method="first"), q, labels=False)
    g=d.groupby("bin");
    x=g[col].mean(); y=g.apply(lambda z:(z[wcol]*z[f"pnl_{tau}"]).sum()/z[wcol].sum())
    return x,y
preds=["liq_aligned_all_5s","same_side_flow_5s","micro_signal_bps","imbalance",
       "spread_bps","absret_60s_bps"]
fig,axes=plt.subplots(2,3,figsize=(15,8))
for ax,col in zip(axes.flat, preds):
    for sym,c in zip(meta["symbols"],[C['binance'],C['accent']]):
        x,y=cond_markout(samp[sym], col, 30, clip=(0.005,0.995))
        ax.plot(x,y,marker='o',ms=3,label=sym,color=c)
    ax.axhline(0,ls='--',c='k',lw=.8); ax.set_title(f"E[pnl_30 | {col}]  (turnover-weighted)")
    ax.set_xlabel(col); ax.set_ylabel("markout bps")
axes.flat[0].legend()
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

1.2.4 Regime structure — data-driven market regimes & their markout¶

In [13]:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
sym="btcusdt"; s=samp[sym].copy()
regf=["absret_60s_bps","spread_bps","liq_mag_all_30s","taker_imb_30s","liq_count_all_5s"]
X=s[regf].replace([np.inf,-np.inf],np.nan).dropna()
Xs=StandardScaler().fit_transform(np.log1p(np.abs(X))*np.sign(X))
km=KMeans(4, n_init=5, random_state=0).fit(Xs)
s2=s.loc[X.index].copy(); s2["regime"]=km.labels_
prof=s2.groupby("regime").agg(absret=("absret_60s_bps","median"),spread=("spread_bps","median"),
      liqmag=("liq_mag_all_30s","median"),imb=("taker_imb_30s","mean"),
      share=("regime","size"))
prof["share"]/=prof["share"].sum()
for tau in cc.TAUS:
    prof[f"pnl_{tau}"]=s2.groupby("regime").apply(lambda z:(z["w"]*z[f"pnl_{tau}"]).sum()/z["w"].sum())
names={r:n for r,n in zip(prof.sort_values("absret").index,["calm","normal","active","stress"])}
prof.index=[names[i] for i in prof.index]
display(prof.sort_values("absret").style.format("{:.3f}"))

1.2.5 Signal-to-noise on the markout targets & 1.2.6 stationarity¶

In [14]:
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(13,4))
# SNR: variance of conditional mean (binned by combo signal) vs total variance
ax=axes[0]; rows=[]
for sym in meta["symbols"]:
    s=samp[sym]
    for tau in cc.TAUS:
        x=(-s["liq_aligned_all_5s"]-s["same_side_flow_5s"]).rank()
        d=pd.DataFrame({"sig":pd.qcut(x,20,labels=False),"y":s[f"pnl_{tau}"],"w":s["w"]}).dropna()
        cm=d.groupby("sig").apply(lambda z:(z.w*z.y).sum()/z.w.sum())
        snr=cm.var()/d["y"].var()
        rows.append(dict(symbol=sym,tau=tau,snr_x1e4=snr*1e4,
                         target_std=d["y"].std(),target_mean=d["y"].mean()))
snr=pd.DataFrame(rows); display(snr)
ax.bar([f"{r.symbol[:3]}-{r.tau}" for r in snr.itertuples()], snr["snr_x1e4"], color=C['accent'])
ax.set_title("predictable variance share of markout  (×1e-4)"); ax.set_ylabel("explained var fraction ×1e4")
# stationarity: daily PnL_all series + ADF
ax=axes[1]
for sym,c in zip(meta["symbols"],[C['binance'],C['accent']]):
    d=daily[daily.symbol==sym].sort_values("day")
    ax.plot(d["day"], d["pnl_all_30"], label=f"{sym} pnl30/day", color=c)
    adf=adfuller(d["pnl_all_30"].dropna())[1]
    print(f"{sym}: daily PnL_all_30 ADF p={adf:.3f}  mean={d['pnl_all_30'].mean():+.3f}  std={d['pnl_all_30'].std():.3f}")
ax.axhline(0,ls='--',c='k',lw=1); ax.legend(); ax.set_title("daily turnover-weighted markout (PnL_all_30)")
plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(),rotation=30,ha='right'); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

Tier 1.3 — Advanced exploration¶

Price impact, side-imbalance × liquidations, liquidation heatmap, cross-exchange lead–lag¶

1.3.1 Order-book price impact — Kyle's λ and microprice predictiveness¶

In [16]:
# Kyle lambda: regress forward mid change on signed clipped volume over fixed clock bins.
sym="btcusdt"; trd,bbo,_,_=st.read_day(st.data_paths(DATA,sym),liveday)
bb=cc.add_mid(bbo); bts=bb["timestamp"].to_numpy(np.int64); midv=bb["mid"].to_numpy(float)
tt=trd["timestamp"].to_numpy(np.int64)
s=np.where(trd["side"].str.lower().to_numpy()=="buy",1.0,-1.0)
w=np.minimum(trd["price"].to_numpy()*trd["amount"].to_numpy(),1e5)
binid=(tt//( 1*US ))  # 1-second bins
sf=pd.Series(s*w).groupby(binid).sum()
midstart=pd.Series(cc._asof_strict_before((sf.index.values*US), bts, midv))
midend=pd.Series(cc._asof_strict_before(((sf.index.values+1)*US), bts, midv))
dmid=((midend.values-midstart.values)/midstart.values*1e4)
dfk=pd.DataFrame({"sf":sf.values/1e6,"dmid":dmid}).replace([np.inf,-np.inf],np.nan).dropna()
import scipy.stats as ss
lam=ss.linregress(dfk["sf"],dfk["dmid"])
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(13,4))
ax=axes[0]; ax.scatter(dfk["sf"],dfk["dmid"],s=3,alpha=.2,color=C['neutral'])
xs=np.linspace(dfk["sf"].quantile(.01),dfk["sf"].quantile(.99),50)
ax.plot(xs, lam.intercept+lam.slope*xs, color=C['sell'])
ax.set_title(f"Kyle λ: Δmid(bps) vs signed $M/s  (λ={lam.slope:.3f} bps per $1M, R²={lam.rvalue**2:.3f})")
ax.set_xlabel("signed flow $M / s"); ax.set_ylabel("Δmid bps (next 1s)")
# microprice predictiveness: does (micro-mid) predict next mid move?
ax=axes[1]
md_dev=(bb["microprice"].to_numpy()-midv)/midv*1e4
fut=cc._asof_backward(bts+1*US, bts, midv)
fwd=(fut-midv)/midv*1e4
dd=pd.DataFrame({"dev":md_dev,"fwd":fwd}).replace([np.inf,-np.inf],np.nan).dropna()
dd["b"]=pd.qcut(dd["dev"].rank(method="first"),20,labels=False)
g=dd.groupby("b").mean()
ax.plot(g["dev"],g["fwd"],marker="o",ms=3,color=C['accent']); ax.axhline(0,ls='--',c='k',lw=.7)
ax.plot(g["dev"],g["dev"],ls=":",c='gray',label="y=x")
ax.set_title("microprice deviation predicts next-1s mid move"); ax.set_xlabel("(micro-mid) bps"); ax.set_ylabel("fwd mid bps"); ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

1.3.4 Cross-exchange lead–lag — does Bybit liquidation flow predict Binance moves?¶

In [19]:
# Event study: align Binance mid around large Bybit liquidation bursts (post +200ms availability).
sym="btcusdt"; horizons=[-5,-2,-1,0,1,2,5,10,30]
days=[int(pd.Timestamp(d,tz="UTC").value//1000) for d in
      ["2025-12-10","2025-12-20","2026-01-05","2026-01-15","2026-02-03","2026-02-20"]]
curves={"bybit_buy":[],"bybit_sell":[]}
for day in days:
    trd,bbo,lB,lY=st.read_day(st.data_paths(DATA,sym),day)
    bb=cc.add_mid(bbo); bts=bb["timestamp"].to_numpy(np.int64); midv=bb["mid"].to_numpy(float)
    lY=lY.copy(); lY["notional"]=lY["price"]*lY["amount"]
    big=lY[lY["notional"]>=lY["notional"].quantile(.95)]
    for _,r in big.iterrows():
        t0=r["timestamp"]; m0=cc._asof_strict_before(np.array([t0]),bts,midv)[0]
        if not np.isfinite(m0): continue
        row=[(cc._asof_backward(np.array([t0+h*US]),bts,midv)[0]/m0-1)*1e4 for h in horizons]
        curves["bybit_buy" if r["side"].lower()=="buy" else "bybit_sell"].append(row)
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,4.2))
for k,c in [("bybit_buy",C['buy']),("bybit_sell",C['sell'])]:
    arr=np.array(curves[k]);
    if len(arr)==0: continue
    mean=np.nanmean(arr,axis=0); se=np.nanstd(arr,axis=0)/np.sqrt(len(arr))
    ax.plot(horizons,mean,marker="o",label=f"{k} (n={len(arr)})",color=c)
    ax.fill_between(horizons,mean-2*se,mean+2*se,alpha=.2,color=c)
ax.axvline(0,ls='--',c='k',lw=1); ax.axhline(0,ls=':',c='gray'); ax.set_xlabel("seconds relative to Bybit liq (already +200ms lagged)")
ax.set_ylabel("Binance mid move (bps)"); ax.set_title(f"{sym}: Binance mid response around large Bybit liquidations")
ax.legend(); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

Executive summary, actionable insights, limitations & data caveats¶

What the data says. A passive Binance maker filled on every print is structurally adversely selected: turnover-weighted markout-PnL is negative at all horizons even after the +0.5 bps rebate. But the loss is not uniform — and crucially, the maker is compensated for absorbing forced flow: trades filled in the direction of recent (cross-venue) liquidation pressure (selling into forced buying) earn positive markout because the cascade over-shoots and mean-reverts. The adverse states are the opposite — fills against the cascade (catching the falling knife) and, more weakly, micro-adverse fills. High-volatility / wide-spread / near-liquidation regimes carry a liquidity premium, not a penalty, for the maker who takes the right side.

Actionable insights for Tasks 2–3.

  1. The single most promising discriminator is direction-relative liquidation alignment (Binance+Bybit, 1–5 s windows / EWMA): KEEP fills that absorb the cascade. Reinforced by microprice signal and fill-distance-from-mid. These are monotone in markout and economically large (several bps).
  2. Bybit leads Binance even after the mandatory +200 ms lag → a genuine, causal, usable feature.
  3. Because per-trade SNR is ~1e-4, edge must be harvested by selecting a small high-quality subset (the Score/turnover-floor framing), not by predicting every trade — and any apparent edge must survive rigorous out-of-sample, multiple-testing-aware validation (Task 3).

Limitations & data caveats.

  • L1 only: booktickers give top-of-book; no depth/queue → impact & true microprice depth are approximated.
  • No funding-rate / open-interest series: funding timing is used, not the rate level (a requested-but-absent dimension).
  • 3-month, single macro-regime window (Dec 2025–Feb 2026): conclusions may not extrapolate to other regimes; the hidden test is on different dates.
  • Markout is frictionless: mid-to-mid forward PnL with a fixed rebate — no queue position, latency, fees beyond rebate, partial fills, or market impact of our own fills. Real maker PnL ≤ markout.
  • Forward-fill mid at t+τ can be stale in data gaps; right-edge trades (t+τ past data end) are excluded per spec.
  • Sampling: population statistics use the full tape via a streaming causal pass; high-resolution plots use a uniform per-day systematic sample (~0.7 M rows/symbol) — verified unbiased for the moments shown.
  • Reproducibility: every number flows from lib/cmf_core.py (audited against the official spec) and lib/factory.py (one causal pass); re-run python lib/factory.py then this notebook top-to-bottom.
